The man likely prevails because when the woman conveyed her house to the man, the easement was extinguished by merger—the man then owned both the dominant and servient estates, and the easement could not survive this unity of ownership. When the man later conveyed the house to the purchaser, the extinguished easement did not pass, regardless of the warranty deed or the purchaser's later discovery of the path.

CONFIDENCE: 90
